hero.body: Berths, tugs, pilots and terminals plan each vessel call together, and everyone sees changes as they happen.

preview.title: Port state
preview.toastBody: Berth, tugs and pilot for Nile Star

landing.statement: A port is many independent parties sharing the same berths, channel, tugs and pilots. ATLANTECH looks at all of their requests together, recommends one coordinated plan, and people approve it before it runs.

request.title: Request
request.body: The berthing request and cargo data arrive in one place.

window.title: Safe entry window
window.body: Weather, tide and channel depth give the safe windows, and staff confirm one.

recommend.title: Recommendation
recommend.body: Berth, tugs and pilot are proposed with their reasons, and staff confirm or adjust them.
recommend.status: Berth B-03, 2 tugs and a pilot

execute.title: Execution
execute.body: Teams carry out the plan and every move is tracked live.

features.title: Everything a vessel call needs.
features.body: One shared picture for the port authority, pilots, tugs and terminals.

requests.title: Berthing requests
requests.body: Submit, review and approve each request and follow it through its whole lifecycle.

windows.title: Safe entry windows
windows.body: Weather, tide and channel depth turn into safe windows and clearly blocked periods.

recommendations.title: Smart recommendations
recommendations.body: Ranked berth, tug and pilot options, each with the reason it was chosen.

resources.title: Tugs and pilots
resources.body: Rosters and assignments in one place, with no double booking across departments.

yard.title: Container yard
yard.body: BAPLIE files and yard placement suggestions for the container terminal.

tracking.title: Live tracking
tracking.body: Plans update the moment something changes, and deviations show up right away.

roles.title: Built for everyone in the port.
roles.body: Each role sees only the pages and terminals it works with.

footer.about: Intelligent port operations: one live picture for berths, tugs, pilots and terminals.

accounts.a: Your port administrator creates every account and gives you a one-time password. You choose your own password the first time you sign in.

offline.q: Does it work on the quay or at sea?
offline.a: Pilots, tug masters and supervisors use the tablet app. It keeps working without a connection and sends updates as soon as it's back online.

languages.a: Arabic and English, with a right-to-left layout for Arabic. Anyone can switch language at any time.

data.a: On your port's own servers, inside the port network. Each terminal operator sees only its own cargo, plans and costs.

decisions.q: Does the system decide on its own?
decisions.a: No. It recommends entry windows, berths, tugs and pilots and explains why, and port staff approve every plan before it runs.

problem.title: Every party plans alone. The whole port pays for it.
problem.body: Port authority, pilotage, tugs and terminals each plan their own resources correctly, yet the port still suffers conflicts and delays.

isolated.title: Isolated planning
isolated.body: Each party optimises its own resources, so clashes over shared berths, tugs and pilots only show up on the day.

future.title: No view of what is coming
future.body: Upcoming arrivals, cargo needs and demand from other terminals are not anticipated.

sea.title: Planning blind to the sea
sea.body: Tide, wind, waves and visibility change safe berthing limits by the hour, yet windows are rarely planned against forecasts.

problem.result: The result: vessels wait, tidal windows are missed and one delay spreads to the next.

systems.title: Works with the systems you already run.
systems.body: ATLANTECH sits above your terminal and port systems and never replaces them. People approve every plan before it is sent for execution.
systems.principle: ATLANTECH recommends and coordinates. Your existing systems execute.
systems.fieldExample: pilots, tug masters and supervisors on tablets

security.title: Runs inside your port.
security.body: Every port gets the same system as its own installation. Ports differ by configuration, not by code.

server.title: Your own server
server.body: A dedicated installation on the port's own server, inside the port network.

data.title: Data stays in the port
data.body: Operational data never reaches the central platform, which only manages licences.

learning.title: Learns from your port only
learning.body: The AI improves from your port's own outcomes. No model or data is shared between ports.

scale.title: Scales by configuration
scale.body: From 1 terminal and 5 berths up to 10 terminals and 50 berths, with no code changes.

security.reference: Designed with Damietta Port as the reference case
